name: Sitagliptin
route_note: oral tablet once daily; dose reduced in kidney impairment
owner: Merck & Co. (MSD); generics in some markets

discovery.by: Merck Research Laboratories (team including Ann Weber)
discovery.note: Designed as a selective DPP-4 inhibitor after earlier non-selective compounds showed toxicity linked to DPP-8/9 inhibition.

tagline: The first DPP-4 inhibitor: a weight-neutral pill that boosts the body's own incretins
summary: Sitagliptin inhibits the enzyme DPP-4, prolonging the action of the gut hormones GLP-1 and GIP so that insulin secretion rises and glucagon falls when glucose is high. Approved in 2006 as the first gliptin, it is weight-neutral, carries little risk of hypoglycaemia and was shown neutral for cardiovascular outcomes in TECOS.
mechanism: The incretin hormones GLP-1 and GIP are released from the gut after meals and amplify glucose-dependent insulin secretion, but are inactivated within minutes by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4). Sitagliptin competitively and selectively inhibits DPP-4, roughly doubling active incretin levels.

Higher incretin levels increase insulin secretion and suppress glucagon in a glucose-dependent manner, lowering fasting and post-meal glucose without the hypoglycaemia typical of sulfonylureas. Unlike GLP-1 receptor agonists, physiological incretin levels produce little effect on appetite or weight.
uses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, monotherapy or combination with metformin, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones or insulin

history.title: First gliptin approved
history.detail: FDA approves Januvia in October 2006; EU approval follows in 2007.

history.title: Janumet
history.detail: A fixed-dose combination with metformin is approved.

history.title: Pancreatitis labelling
history.detail: FDA adds information on post-marketing reports of acute pancreatitis to the label.

history.title: TECOS
history.detail: The TECOS trial in 14,671 patients shows no increase in major cardiovascular events or heart-failure hospitalisation.

history.title: European generics
history.detail: Generic sitagliptin enters EU markets after regulatory exclusivity and patent protection end.

facts: Januvia was the first DPP-4 inhibitor approved anywhere (FDA, October 2006).
Sitagliptin is excreted mostly unchanged by the kidneys, so doses are reduced when eGFR falls.
